title: Basie's 1936 personnel: brass, reeds, Caughey Roberts, Claude Williams
summary: Jones names the four brass and the saxophones of the band that came to New York in 1936, with Caughey Roberts replaced by Earl Warren, and Claude Williams on guitar and violin.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Just digress just a second and go back before '44 because I'm trying to start in the 40's now. What was the trumpet section the band became in New York in 1936?
Joe Keyes, Tatti, Carl Smith -
Tatti, Tatti - who was
He was a trumpet player...
Was Tatti Carl Smith?
Yes, his name was Carl Smith.
But you called him Tatti
Yeh, we all - he had a nickname Tatti ... and Buck Clayton. Dan Minor, that's all.
One trombone.

Wait just a moment. I did say we had Joe Keyes, Taddy, Dan Minor. That was the brass, four brass. We had Jack Washington; we had Lester Young, Herschel Evans, and we had Caughey Roberts. Caughey Roberts was from Los Angeles.
JONES 78
What did he play?

First alto, excellent musician, and he stayed just for a little while and then they picked up Earl Warren out of Cincinnati, because Earl Warren I'm pretty sure was playing with Al Sears in Cincinnati at the Ferguson Hotel there.
May I ask you who Caughey Roberts was?
Caughy, C-a-u-h. His father had the bath houses out there in California at the time.
Warren took his place in your band?
Earl replaced Caughy Roberts and Caughy went on back to California. Claude Williams was playing guitar and violin, which he's alive today and he still was an excellent violinist.
Did they use a violin at all in the band?
Sometimes we did; of course we did. Claude was a little older than Stuff Smith.
Can you remember anything that he might have played on a violin in the band?
